author: claude-opus-5 (knowledge cutoff May 2026; event window 2026-06-27..2026-07-19 is post-cutoff)
shock: US-Iran escalation, Strait of Hormuz disrupted. Oil +6% Brent / +9% WTI daily, ~+11% weekly. Dollar stronger, government bond yields climbing, gold falling as Fed rate-hike bets revive.
reasoning: Two transmission channels, both cross-sectional. (1) OIL: a supply shock via Hormuz raises crude, which is a windfall for producers/services and a direct cost shock for fuel-intensive transport. (2) RATES: the quotes say the oil spike de-anchored inflation expectations and revived hike bets, with yields up and gold down. That is a discount-rate shock, which hits long-duration assets hardest - high-multiple growth, REITs, utilities, long bonds. Names exposed to NEITHER channel and with domestic, non-fuel, non-duration cash flows should be the least moved.

most_exposed.why: US airline; jet fuel is the largest variable cost and the quotes explicitly note airfares rising
same fuel channel, plus long-haul routes over affected airspace
domestic US airline, historically the most fuel-hedged - included deliberately as a within-industry contrast
European low-cost carrier; fuel plus European equity weakness noted in the quotes
integrated major; direct crude price beneficiary
integrated major with large trading arm; benefits from dislocation as well as level
oil services; activity and pricing lever off crude
US shale E&P; highest torque to crude of the producers here
defense prime; active US strikes on Iran
long-duration Treasuries; the rates channel is a direct hit and the quotes state yields climbed

least_exposed.why: US shell eggs; domestic, food-price driven, no fuel or duration channel
coffee trading micro-cap; own commodity cycle, unrelated to crude or rates
pet insurance; domestic subscription cash flows
insurtech; idiosyncratic, no oil or Hormuz linkage
campus bookstores; domestic retail, own distress cycle
packaged food; defensive, domestic, low duration
US foodservice distribution - note this one has a fuel cost channel, so it is the weakest member of this list
small US regional bank; domestic lending, no Hormuz channel

falsifiable_prediction: Mean |standardised abnormal move| over the window is HIGHER for most_exposed than for least_exposed, and higher than the universe mean. If the gap is <= 0 the reasoning channel adds nothing.
known_weaknesses: All 12 extracted events are the same macro story, so this is effectively ONE shock, not 12 independent tests.
least_exposed is skewed to micro-caps, which carry high idiosyncratic vol; standardising by each name's own trailing vol is meant to neutralise that but may not fully.
23-day corpus, 264-name universe: a pilot, not a verdict.
